content.comment_body: Hello. I'm interested in purchasing a [product_name] module that operates at 24VDC input, with relay outputs, compatible with AM2 RTD, and supports all the features available in the FS4 functionality of [product_name] at [version_no]. Could you advise where I could locate this model? Alternatively, do I need to use a 220V version to have a display and all desired functionalities?

The 230VAC [product_name], regardless of display, cannot accept 24VDC input. The main distinction between a 230RCE version and a 24RCE version involves the voltage supported by their digital inputs. Please outline in detail what you're trying to achieve.
You updated your post and changed the description significantly from your original version.

All [product_name] base modules offer AM2 RTD connectivity. For 24VDC inputs, these [product_name] variants are available: 12/24 RCE, 24 RCE, 24 CE. Models without displays include: 12/24 RCEo, 24 RCEo, and 24 CEo.
These are the order numbers for current [product_name] modules at [version_no].

I'm unfamiliar with some of these details—thanks for clarifying. Could you explain what the 0BA8 platform is? What do terms like FS4-5-6 refer to? How do these combine, and why are some products designated as 0BA1? What does this imply for their usage?
Why can't I locate the product with article number [article_no] anywhere?
I see applications related to [version_no] here. How do I implement them? [url]
If you're referring to the manual for the latest [product_name] module at [version_no], you can find it via this link: [document]. I’ve attached a summary regarding the history of the 0BA8 modules.

So, you're suggesting that 0BA0 is essentially the 0BA8 for 2021? If so, why can't I use And(Edge) or And logic with four inputs, for example? What's required to run a program built with FS4 hardware type on [product_name] at [version_no]?

[company_name] has updated order numbering. With the release of [product_name] at [version_no], the 0BA8 segment at the end of the order number was removed, and 08 now indicates a 0BA8 module. Examples: [product_name] 8.0: 0BA8 first generation: [article_no]; [product_name] 8.1: 0BA8 second generation: [article_no]; [product_name] 8.2: 0BA8 third generation: [article_no]; [product_name] 8.3: 0BA8 fourth generation: [article_no].

After thorough troubleshooting, I found that updating the firmware resolved the issue. I installed the latest version from [url] and now the module connects using FS4 rather than 0BA0. Previously, you posted about this solution—perhaps it should be made a sticky post instead of the legacy update. The manuals lack clarity regarding FS4 features, which are only implied (for example: "192.168.000.003 is the new FS4"). The part number is now 0BA1, causing further confusion when installing programs, as FS4 programs cannot connect directly—you need to create new ones for 0BA0/1 versions.
Your posts are confusing because the explanation changes with each new question. You haven't specified which exact [product_name] module you have (including the order number).

I possess a 24RCE module with order number [article_no]. Initially, I assumed software limitations were the cause, but after attempting a program update, I updated the firmware instead, which addressed the issues. I prefer to avoid 220V due to safety concerns. Through your replies, I learned where to look—the firmware update improved more than just security features.
You can upgrade to the latest firmware. Here is product information about the firmware update for [product_name] at [version_no], addressing security vulnerability CVE-2020-7593.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report significant confusion about the different variants of [product_name] modules, especially regarding hardware revisions (such as 0BA8 and 0BA1), compatible input voltages (24VDC versus 230VAC), and how hardware features relate to newest logic functions and expansion modules like AM2 RTD. Terms like FS4 and changing product codes add complexity, making it challenging for users to select the right module. Inconsistent terminology and documentation gaps further increase uncertainty among users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a clear guide mapping hardware versions to specific features, input types, and compatibility, enabling them to easily identify and purchase the appropriate [product_name] module for their needs, including support for AM2 RTD extension modules and advanced logic functions described in newer documentation.
